newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian parents threaten another mass march.
newsitem.headline: Belgian parents threaten another mass march.

text.p: The parents of two of Belgium's sexually abused and murdered children called on Thursday for the country's interior minister to resign, threatening a new mass rally in Brussels if he refused, Belgian radio said.

"I think the minister of the interior should resign," said Gino Russo, father of Melissa whose body was found buried alongside that of friend Julie Lejeune three months ago on a property owned by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.
"If he doesn't we will organise...a red march", Julie's father Denis added.

Brussels was brought to a standstill last month when 250,000 people took to the streets wearing or carrying white to signify sympathy with the parents of the four girls so far found dead and the many others missing in Belgium's child abduction, sexual abuse and murder scandal.

The parents of Julie and Melissa, abducted in June last year, hold Interior Minister Johann vande Lanotte responsible for bungling and inefficiency among the police -- and particularly the gendarmerie -- that has come to light during the renewed inquiries.
Vande Lanotte told RTBF television he refused to be a scapegoat, adding that it was in fact Justice Minister Stefaan de Clerck who was responsible for the gendarmerie.

Belgium has been in turmoil since the arrest of Dutroux and several associates -- including his second wife Michelle Martin -- in mid-August, and the subsequent rescue of two young girls and the discovery of the bodies of four more.

Allegations of a high level cover-up have been rife -- fuelled by the removal from the case last month of the magistrate leading the investigations, accused of having compromised himself by accepting a free pasta dinner from an organisation dedicated to helping families of missing children.
The ruling by Belgium's highest court sparked demonstratons across the country and fired emotions at the October 20 white march.

The parents of the dead and some of the missing children on Wednesday lodged a formal appeal against the decision to remove magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte -- seen as one of the few honest magistrates in the country -- from the case.
The government has set up an inquiry into the earlier investigations and promised rapid reforms of the judicial system, particularly the political promotion of magistrates.
It is also looking at creating a Federal Bureau of Investigation to supplement the existing territorially and linguistically-divided police and gendarmerie forces.
